summary: Write five Introductions on different narrative threads, then critique them through three different lenses

drafts.text:
The elementary random variable in an ion channel recording is the dwell time, how long a channel stays open or shut before switching. What an experiment sees of it is set by one ratio: the gating events a channel makes in one acquisition interval, that interval in units of the relaxation time. Call it the events per sample. Well below one, a sample sits inside one sojourn and kinetics come from duration distributions (Neher & Steinbach 1977; Colquhoun & Hawkes 1981). Far above one they average away within each sample, the current relaxes deterministically, and kinetics come from differential equations fitted by least squares (Hodgkin & Huxley 1952).

Most macroscopic patch-clamp records sit in neither regime: a few hundred to a few thousand channels, openings unresolvable, averaging incomplete. The dwell times leave a fluctuation around the mean, correlated over the relaxation time, carrying what the mean cannot: channel number and unitary current enter it as a product, inseparable there. The standard analysis is least squares on that mean anyway, deterministic with a root-mean-square objective in the four approaches surveyed by Clerx et al. (2019), and IonBench excludes stochastic models (Owen et al. 2025). Ignoring the correlation usually leaves the point estimate standing while corrupting the count of independent residuals behind every confidence interval.

Using that correlation is old: stationary noise read as a Lorentzian spectrum, the Fourier transform of the autocovariance, gave rates and unitary conductances (Katz & Miledi 1970, 1972), and Anderson & Stevens (1973) got a conductance and a closing rate jointly, with standard errors. The exact non-stationary two-time covariance for identical independent channels came a decade later, from ensembles of 256 to 504 sweeps (Conti et al. 1980; Sigworth 1981). What is missing is validity, the range over which a likelihood reports its uncertainty honestly.

The likelihoods that followed differ in how much of it each keeps. Milescu, Akk & Sachs (2005) keep the gating variance at every sample and drop the dependence between successive measurements. Celentano & Hawkes (2004) keep the full two-time covariance, at a cost climbing steeply with sample count, and are applied to a hundred or two selected points. Moffatt (2007) reads the occupancy as Bayesian, the state probability vector measuring the observer's uncertainty rather than population frequencies, which is explicitly what allows conditioning on each new datum and propagation at linear cost, parameters following by maximum likelihood. Stepanyuk et al. (2011) restore the full covariance at near-linear cost with a semiseparable representation. Münch et al. (2022) carry the recursion into Bayesian inference over the parameters, with state-dependent open-channel noise. Moffatt & Pierdominici-Sottile (2025) condition the interval-averaged observable on the states at both ends of each interval. The order walks two axes: how much gating stochasticity is modelled, from nothing to the per-sample variance to its correlation in time, and whether an observation is a point or an interval average.

All of it is published, implemented and almost unused. The published explanation is cost (Del Core & Mirams 2025). A hypothesis, labelled as such: no fast algorithm integrated the current over the acquisition interval, leaving the fast members wrong about the observable and the right one unable to run a whole record.

Adopting one costs something. Least squares predicts the trace from the parameters alone, so its residual reads against outside knowledge, in amplitude against what gating variance and baseline noise should deliver, in time correlation against what the scheme leaves out. A recursive likelihood predicts each interval from the parameters and the data already seen, so the trace follows the record by construction, whether the scheme is right, wrong, or the code broken, and standardising the residual against its own variance makes both readings internal. That blindness covers two questions an experimenter cannot separate, whether the approximation is adequate and whether the code is correct.

The apparatus is classical. At the true parameters the score, the gradient of the log-likelihood, averages to zero over replicate recordings, and its covariance across them equals the Fisher information the likelihood reports, so a gap between the spread a method delivers and the uncertainty it claims is misspecification made quantitative (Godambe 1960; Huber 1967; White 1982). What this class of model adds is a forward process that simulates exactly while its likelihood cannot, so the simulator supplies ground truth. The distortion runs both ways, some approximations overstating the information the data carry and others understating it, so each has a domain of validity.

Three quantities fix position on the map. The number of channels sets how close the aggregate occupancy is to Gaussian, a different question from resolution. The acquisition interval in relaxation times is the events per sample. Instrumental noise is in units of the gating noise at fixed spectral density, so a shorter interval raises the noise per sample and leaves the noise per unit bandwidth unchanged. The scheme is two-state at open probability one half, the most favourable case for a Gaussian occupancy and a lower bound for anything richer. Least squares turns calibrated where instrumental noise dominates, honest there about strictly less, with only the product of channel number and unitary current identified. The score identity needs an ensemble of replicates no reader has for their own experiment, so we hand back a single measurement on their residual, its correlation time in samples, the events per sample again, locating them on the map. Which to prefer, and when, is not settled here.

With one channel in the patch, dwell times are read off the record and the rates come from their distributions (Neher & Steinbach 1977; Colquhoun & Hawkes 1981). In the currents underlying an action potential the durations average away, the current relaxes deterministically, and the rates come from differential equations fitted by least squares (Hodgkin & Huxley 1952). Most macroscopic recordings sit between: a few hundred to a few thousand channels, individual openings unresolvable, averaging incomplete, so the dwell times leave a fluctuation around the mean, correlated over the relaxation time.

That fluctuation carries what the mean cannot: channel number and unitary current enter the mean current as a product, so no fit to the mean separates them. Fitting is done on the mean anyway, deterministically and by root-mean-square in the approaches surveyed by Clerx et al. (2019), with IonBench excluding stochastic models (Owen et al. 2025). Ignoring the correlation usually leaves the point estimate intact; what it damages is the count of independent residuals, the number turning a residual sum of squares into a confidence interval.

Least squares has survived for a reason worth conceding first: its prediction comes from the parameters alone, so the residual can be read directly, and twice, its amplitude against what gating variance and baseline noise should give, its correlation in time against what the fit leaves out. Both readings appeal to knowledge from outside the fit, which makes them checks.

Correlation-based kinetics is not new: stationary Lorentzian spectra gave a unitary conductance and a closing rate with standard errors on both (Katz & Miledi 1970, 1972; Anderson & Stevens 1973), the exact non-stationary two-time covariance following a decade later (Conti et al. 1980; Sigworth 1981). Whole-record likelihoods keep different amounts: the per-sample gating variance, successive samples treated as independent (Milescu, Akk & Sachs 2005); the full covariance, at a cost confining it to a hundred or two points (Celentano & Hawkes 2004); a recursion from a Bayesian reading of the occupancy, where the state probability vector measures the observer's uncertainty rather than the frequencies of a hypothetical population, which is what lets it be conditioned on each datum and propagated at linear cost, parameters by maximum likelihood (Moffatt 2007); the full covariance again at near-linear cost (Stepanyuk et al. 2011); that recursion carried into Bayesian inference over the parameters, with state-dependent open-channel noise (Münch et al. 2022); and the interval-averaged observable conditioned on the states at both ends of each interval (Moffatt & Pierdominici-Sottile 2025). The sequence walks two axes: how much gating stochasticity is modelled, and whether an observation is a point or an interval average.

They are published, implemented, available and almost unused. The published explanation is cost (Del Core & Mirams 2025). As a hypothesis: with no fast algorithm integrating the current over the acquisition interval, the fast members were wrong about the observable and the one right about it could not run a whole record.

Each also takes the two readings away. A recursive likelihood predicts each interval from the parameters and from the data already seen, so the previous sample enters the prediction of the next and the trace follows the record by construction, whether the scheme is right, wrong, or the code broken. It also standardises each residual against its predicted variance, so both readings become statements of internal consistency. Take a model with no kinetics, one that says each sample equals the last plus noise: sampled fast enough it predicts almost perfectly and knows nothing. A criterion that model passes cannot separate a working implementation from a broken one, let alone a good approximation from a bad one. That is the criterion these likelihoods leave. Algorithm and code are one question, which the experimenter cannot separate and has no reason to.

What is missing is the measurement. Its apparatus is classical: at the true parameters the score, the gradient of the log-likelihood, averages to zero across replicate recordings, and its covariance equals the Fisher information the likelihood reports (Godambe 1960; Huber 1967; White 1982). Departure from either is misspecification: the error bar the fit prints is not the spread it delivers. Both are checkable here because the forward process simulates exactly while its likelihood cannot. Three quantities set position on the map, two dimensionless: channel number, the acquisition interval in units of the relaxation time, and instrumental noise in units of gating noise at fixed spectral density, so a shorter interval raises noise per sample and not per bandwidth. The scheme is two-state at open probability one half, the friendliest case for a Gaussian occupancy and so a lower bound on the error for anything richer.

Every member is an approximation, so the measurement returns a domain: distortion runs both ways, some reporting more information than the data carry and others less, and the question is where a likelihood is faithful. Least squares becomes calibrated once instrumental noise exceeds gating noise, its reported interval matching its delivered spread. Calibration is not adequacy: the information matrix is rank deficient there, the product of channel number and unitary current all that is identified, so it is honest about strictly less. The identity needs an ensemble of replicates at one design point, out of reach for a single experiment. What the map hands back is one measurement on the reader's own residual, enough to place that experiment on it and ask whether the interval a fit prints is the one it delivers.

In a single-channel recording the durations of openings and shuttings are observed directly, and their distributions give the rates (Neher and Steinbach 1977; Colquhoun and Hawkes 1981). In the currents behind an action potential the durations average away over so many channels that the current relaxes deterministically, and the rates come from differential equations fitted by least squares (Hodgkin and Huxley 1952).

What separates the two is the number of gating events inside one acquisition interval. Below one event per sample, openings resolve singly; far above, the trace is smooth. Most macroscopic recordings sit between, a few hundred to a few thousand channels, where the dwell times leave a fluctuation around the mean, correlated over the relaxation time, carrying what the mean cannot: channel number and unitary current enter it as a product no fit to the mean can separate.

Standard practice discards it. The four approaches surveyed by Clerx et al. (2019) are least squares on the deterministic mean, and IonBench does not cover optimisation for stochastic models (Owen et al. 2025). The point estimate often survives; the count of independent residuals that turns a residual sum of squares into a confidence interval does not.

The correlation has served kinetics since the 1970s. Lorentzian current spectra under stationary conditions, the Fourier transform of the autocovariance, gave a unitary conductance and a closing rate jointly, with standard errors on both (Katz and Miledi 1970, 1972; Anderson and Stevens 1973); the exact non-stationary two-time covariance for identical independent Markov channels followed a decade later (Conti et al. 1980; Sigworth 1981). What has stayed open is where a given treatment is valid.

A ladder followed. Milescu, Akk and Sachs (2005) keep the gating variance at each sample and drop the dependence between successive ones. Celentano and Hawkes (2004) keep the whole two-time covariance, at a cost that confines it to a hundred or two points. Moffatt (2007) reads the occupancy vector as the observer's uncertainty rather than population frequencies, which lets it be conditioned on each datum and propagated: a filter linear in the record, fitted by maximum likelihood. Stepanyuk et al. (2011) recover the whole covariance at near-linear cost by a semiseparable representation. Münch et al. (2022) take the recursion into Bayesian inference over parameters, with conductance noise growing with the open channels. Moffatt and Pierdominici-Sottile (2025) condition the interval-averaged observable on the states at both ends of each interval. Two things vary along it: how much gating stochasticity the likelihood models, from none to the per-sample variance to its correlation in time, and whether a sample is a point or an average. All of it is published, available and almost unused, with computational cost the published explanation (Del Core and Mirams 2025).

Something else changes as you climb. Least squares predicts from the parameters alone, so the residual can be read directly: its amplitude against what gating variance and baseline noise should give, its correlation in time against what the fit leaves out, both judged from outside the fit. A recursive likelihood predicts each interval from the parameters and from the data already seen, so its predicted trace follows the record by construction whether the scheme is right, wrong, or the code broken, and it standardises the residual against its own predicted variance, turning both readings into internal consistency. A model with no kinetics, saying each sample equals the last plus noise, predicts almost perfectly when sampled fast enough and says nothing. Those readings covered two questions an experimenter cannot separate, whether the approximation is adequate and whether the code is correct, since the tool is the algorithm plus the executable.

The apparatus is classical: at the true parameters the score, the gradient of the log-likelihood, averages to zero over replicate recordings, and its covariance across them equals the Fisher information the likelihood reports (Godambe 1960; Huber 1967; White 1982), so honest error bars match the spread of estimates delivered. They are usable here through an asymmetry: the process simulates exactly while its likelihood cannot be computed exactly, so simulation gives ground truth for what the likelihood approximates. What is new is the measurement.

Three quantities set position on the map, two of them dimensionless: the number of channels, the interval in units of the relaxation time, and the instrumental noise in units of the gating noise, at fixed spectral density, so shortening the interval raises the noise per sample at constant noise per unit bandwidth. The scheme is two-state at open probability one half, the most favourable case for a Gaussian occupancy and a lower bound for anything richer. Every member is misspecified by construction, so what comes back is a domain: where each overstates the information in the data and where it understates it. Least squares becomes calibrated once instrumental noise exceeds gating noise, its interval matching the spread delivered, though its information matrix is rank deficient there, with the product of channel number and unitary current all that stays identified: honest about strictly less. The boundary-conditioned likelihood is one more tool whose place this paper does not settle.

The identity needs an ensemble of replicate recordings at one design point, the level between a single trace and the map that no experimenter has for their own data; what comes back to them is one measurement on their own residual, and placing it asks how many gating events fell into each sample.

drafts.thread: C: the enemy inside the weapon
drafts.text:
In a patch with one channel the dwell time, how long it stays open or shut, is read off the record, and rate constants come from the distributions of those durations (Neher & Steinbach 1977; Colquhoun & Hawkes 1981). In the currents behind an action potential so many channels contribute that the durations average away, the current relaxes deterministically, and kinetics come from differential equations fitted by least squares (Hodgkin & Huxley 1952). Most macroscopic recordings sit in neither place: a few hundred to a few thousand channels, with openings unresolvable and averaging incomplete. The dwell times survive as a fluctuation around the mean, correlated over the channel's relaxation time: a memory in every trace, invisible because nothing in it looks like a dwell time.

That fluctuation carries what the mean cannot: channel number and unitary current enter the mean as a product, so a fit to the mean cannot separate them; their separation is in the fluctuations, in size and in decay. Standard practice fits the mean anyway: the approaches surveyed by Clerx et al. (2019) are deterministic with a root-mean-square objective, and IonBench states that it does not cover optimisation approaches for stochastic models (Owen et al. 2025). Ignoring the correlation leaves the point estimate intact; what it damages is the count of independent residuals that turns a residual sum of squares into a confidence interval.

Kinetics have been read from that correlation since the 1970s: Lorentzian noise spectra, the Fourier transform of the autocovariance, gave a unitary conductance and a closing rate with standard errors on both (Katz & Miledi 1970, 1972; Anderson & Stevens 1973); the exact non-stationary covariance came a decade later (Conti et al. 1980; Sigworth 1981). Milescu, Akk & Sachs (2005) keep the gating variance at every sample and drop the dependence between samples; Celentano & Hawkes (2004) keep the full two-time covariance, at a cost that limits it to a couple of hundred points; Stepanyuk et al. (2011) restore it at near-linear cost with a semiseparable representation. Moffatt (2007) derives a recursive filter from a Bayesian reading of the occupancy, the state probability vector measuring an observer's uncertainty rather than population frequencies, which is what lets it be conditioned on each new datum and propagated at linear cost, parameters coming from maximum likelihood. Münch et al. (2022) carry the recursion into Bayesian inference over the parameters, with noise modelled as open-channel conductance noise; Moffatt & Pierdominici-Sottile (2025) condition the interval-averaged observable on the channel states at both ends of each interval. Ordered by how much correlation each keeps, the sequence climbs toward that memory along two axes: how much gating stochasticity the likelihood models, and whether an observation is a point or an interval average.

These methods are published, implemented, available and almost unused; the published explanation is computational cost (Del Core & Mirams 2025). Climbing toward the memory takes something away. Least squares predicts from the parameters alone, so its residual can be read directly, and twice: amplitude against what gating variance and baseline noise should deliver, correlation in time against what the fit leaves out, both judged from outside the fit. A recursive likelihood predicts each interval from the parameters and from the data already seen, so the previous sample enters the prediction of the next and the predicted trace follows the record by construction, right scheme or wrong, working code or broken; standardising the residual against its predicted variance makes both readings internal consistency checks. The limiting case is a model with no kinetics at all, each sample equal to the last plus noise: sampled fast enough it predicts almost perfectly and says nothing. What must be modelled to recover the information is the same memory that lets a model track the data without earning it, blinding two questions an experimenter cannot separate: whether the approximation is adequate and whether the code is correct.

The apparatus is classical: at the true parameters the score, the gradient of the log-likelihood, averages to zero over replicate recordings, and its covariance across them equals the Fisher information the likelihood reports (Godambe 1960; Huber 1967; White 1982). Departure from either identity is misspecification: the error bar a fit prints is not the spread it delivers over repeats. What is new is the measurement, possible because the forward process can be simulated exactly while its likelihood cannot, so the simulator gives ground truth.

Every member is an approximation, so the measurement returns a domain rather than a verdict, some members overstating the information in the data and others understating it. Three quantities set position on the map, two of them dimensionless: channel number, the acquisition interval in units of the relaxation time, and the instrumental noise in units of the gating noise at fixed spectral density. The scheme is two-state at open probability one half, the most favourable case for a Gaussian occupancy and so a lower bound on the error for anything richer.

The problem has three levels: one trace, an ensemble of replicates at a design point, and the map over design points. The score identity needs the ensemble, a level no reader reaches for their own experiment. What comes back is one measurement on the reader's own residual, locating that experiment on a map whose boundaries are level sets of continuous diagnostics. The interval-conditioned likelihood is one more tool, and when each is preferable is not settled here.

Ion channel kinetics come from two kinds of recording. In a single-channel patch the dwell time in each level is observed directly, and rates follow from the distributions of those durations (Neher and Steinbach 1977; Colquhoun and Hawkes 1981). In the currents behind an action potential those durations average away over so many channels, the current relaxes deterministically, and rates come from differential equations fitted by least squares (Hodgkin and Huxley 1952).

Most macroscopic recordings sit in neither regime. Fit a scheme to a patch of a few hundred to a few thousand channels and you are in the middle: no opening is resolvable, the averaging is incomplete, and a fluctuation survives whose samples are correlated over the channel's relaxation time. Channel number and unitary current enter the mean as a product, so no fit to the mean separates them; what separates them is in the fluctuation.

The correlation has been used for kinetics since the 1970s. Lorentzian power spectra under stationary conditions, the Fourier transform of the autocovariance, gave a unitary conductance and a closing rate with a standard error on each (Katz and Miledi 1970, 1972; Anderson and Stevens 1973), and the exact non-stationary two-time covariance for identical independent Markov channels followed a decade later (Conti et al. 1980; Sigworth 1981). Celentano and Hawkes (2004) keep that full covariance, at a cost confining it to a hundred or two points. Milescu, Akk and Sachs (2005) keep the gating variance at each sample and drop the dependence between successive samples. Moffatt (2007) reads the occupancy vector as the observer's uncertainty rather than population frequencies, which licenses conditioning it on each datum and propagating it forward, at a cost linear in the record. Stepanyuk et al. (2011) restore the full covariance at near-linear cost with a semiseparable representation. Münch et al. (2022) carry the recursion into Bayesian inference over the parameters, modelling noise as state-dependent open-channel conductance. Moffatt and Pierdominici-Sottile (2025) condition the interval-averaged observable on the states at both ends of each interval. The sequence walks two axes: how much gating stochasticity is modelled, from none to per-sample variance to correlation in time, and whether an observation is a point or an interval average.

The standard analysis is still least squares on the deterministic mean: all four approaches surveyed by Clerx et al. (2019) use a root-mean-square objective, and the IonBench benchmark does not cover optimisation for stochastic models (Owen et al. 2025). Ignoring the correlation rarely moves the point estimate; it moves the count of independent residuals that turns a residual sum of squares into a confidence interval. Those likelihoods are published, implemented and almost unused. The published explanation is computational cost (Del Core and Mirams 2025). A further hypothesis, offered as one: no fast algorithm integrated the current over the acquisition interval, leaving the fast members wrong about the observable and the one right about it too slow for whole records.

That class also takes something away. A least-squares prediction comes from the parameters alone, so the residual reads directly against outside knowledge: its amplitude against what gating variance and baseline noise should give, its correlation in time against what the fit leaves out. A recursive likelihood predicts each interval from the parameters and from the data already seen, so the trace follows the record whether the scheme is right, wrong, or the code broken, and standardising each residual by its predicted variance makes both readings internal checks. A model with no kinetics, each sample equal to the last plus noise, passes both. The blindness covers whether the approximation is adequate and whether the code computing it is correct, the tool being the algorithm plus its executable.

The apparatus is classical. At the true parameters the score, the gradient of the log-likelihood, averages to zero across replicate recordings, and its covariance equals the Fisher information the likelihood reports for itself; a gap either way is misspecification, since an approximation can overstate the information in the data as easily as understate it (Godambe 1960; Huber 1967; White 1982). The identities are usable here because the forward process simulates exactly while its likelihood cannot be computed exactly, so the simulator supplies ground truth. What is new is the measurement, and since every member approximates, it returns a domain rather than a verdict.

Three quantities fix position on that map, two dimensionless: channel number, the acquisition interval in units of the channel's relaxation time, and instrumental noise in units of gating noise at fixed spectral density, so shortening the interval raises the noise per sample and leaves the noise per unit bandwidth unchanged. The scheme is two-state at open probability one half, the most favourable case for a Gaussian treatment of the occupancy and a lower bound for anything richer. Least squares becomes calibrated, its interval matching the spread it delivers, once instrumental noise exceeds gating noise; there the information matrix is rank deficient, only the product of channel number and unitary current identified, so it is honest about strictly less. That arm is unfinished.

Open probability, stationary protocols and richer schemes are excluded by that design. The score identity needs an ensemble of replicate recordings at one design point, which no reader has for their own experiment, so we hand back one measurement on their residual that locates them on the map. The new recursion is one more tool on it; which to prefer where is not settled here.

result.structural:
**1. Threads detected.**
INTRO-1 promises a single ratio, the gating events per acquisition interval, as the coordinate that explains everything, and names it in the first paragraph and the last. INTRO-2 runs a concession: least squares earns its survival because its residual is readable from outside the fit, and every rung of the likelihood ladder confiscates that reading, so the missing thing is a measurement. INTRO-3 is a ladder, explicitly signposted ("A ladder followed", "Something else changes as you climb"), ordering the literature by how much correlation each keeps. INTRO-4 runs on one image, memory: the dwell times survive as a memory nothing in the trace looks like, the methods climb toward it, and the same memory that carries the information lets a model track data without earning it. INTRO-5 has no detectable thread. It is a well-ordered inventory: history, ladder, practice, cost, apparatus, design, exclusions. Nothing governs the order, which is the important finding about it.

**2. Most material without strain.**
INTRO-4. It seats the ladder, the blindness, the score identity, the three design quantities and the three-level structure, and only the last two paragraphs sit outside the image. What it skips is the ratio: it says "openings unresolvable, averaging incomplete" and never names what puts a recording there, so the middle regime is described but not located. INTRO-2 places nearly as much but forces its ladder into one semicolon-chained sentence that reads as a bibliography with the argument switched off. INTRO-1 forces its own opening: it declares one ratio decisive, then organizes nothing by it, and drops "What is missing is validity" into the history paragraph where it has nothing to attach to. INTRO-3 leaves its last paragraph dangling as a fragment and leaves "The boundary-conditioned likelihood is one more tool" unattached to anything before it. INTRO-5 skips nothing and forces nothing because it argues nothing; its danglers are "That arm is unfinished" and the exclusions sentence, both landing with no antecedent.

**3. Where each loses the line.**
INTRO-1: at "Using that correlation is old". The ratio disappears there and does not return until the final paragraph, where it reappears as an assertion rather than a payoff, and that final paragraph is a heap of noise units, scheme, calibration, rank deficiency and reader handoff.
INTRO-2: at the ladder paragraph. The concession stops operating for the length of the list and has to be restarted.
INTRO-3: after "Something else changes as you climb". The climb metaphor stops paying, and the closing two paragraphs are stubs bolted on.
INTRO-4: at the apparatus paragraph. Memory never appears again; the final two paragraphs read as an appendix, and "level sets of continuous diagnostics" is an abstraction where the reader needed a number.
INTRO-5: paragraph four. It presents the whole ladder before telling us standard practice ignores the correlation, so the alternatives answer a question the reader has not been given. That inversion is the clearest structural error in the set.

**4. Ranking.**
4, 2, 3, 1, 5. INTRO-5 is bad: a competent list with no argument, in the wrong order. INTRO-1 is bad in a different way, promising an organizing ratio and defaulting on it, which is worse than never promising.

The winner should borrow three things. From 1 and 3, the events-per-sample ratio, used twice: to define the middle regime in paragraph one, and as the reader's handoff at the end, where 3's closing ("placing it asks how many gating events fell into each sample") beats 4's level sets outright. From 2, the explicit concession that least squares survived for a reason, stated before the ladder, so the confiscated readings land as a cost the paper accepts rather than a complaint; and 2's hinge sentence, "What is missing is the measurement", which 4 states only obliquely. From 5, the one sentence nobody else has: what the design excludes (open probability, stationary protocols, richer schemes). And 4 should keep the memory image out of the apparatus paragraph or extend it there, because right now it just stops.
result.attack:
**1. Claims I would challenge**

INTRO-1, "What an experiment sees of it is set by one ratio... Call it the events per sample." Contradicted by its own paragraph 9, "Three quantities fix position on the map." If one ratio sets what the experiment sees, the channel-number axis is decoration. Pick one.

INTRO-1, "The elementary random variable in an ion channel recording is the dwell time." No. The elementary random variable is the state trajectory; dwell times are exponential only per sojourn in a single-channel description, and with multiple open states they are not read off at all.

INTRO-3, "What separates the two is the number of gating events inside one acquisition interval. Below one event per sample, openings resolve singly." False. Openings resolve singly because there is one channel in the patch. Sample a thousand channels at 100 kHz and nothing resolves. INTRO-1 makes the same substitution ("Well below one, a sample sits inside one sojourn"). INTRO-2 is the only draft that gets the discriminator right ("With one channel in the patch").

All three, "At the true parameters the score... averages to zero." Under misspecification there is no true parameter for the model; the score vanishes at the pseudo-true θ*, which is not the simulator's θ. The whole measurement hinges on that distinction and no draft states it. INTRO-1's "misspecification made quantitative" advertises the gap it just papered over.

All three, "fitted by least squares (Hodgkin & Huxley 1952)." Hodgkin and Huxley fitted by hand. A referee in this field will say so.

All three: Godambe 1960 cited for a score identity that is Fisher's. Godambe is estimating functions.

INTRO-1/INTRO-2, "IonBench excludes stochastic models." Owen et al. state they do not cover optimisation approaches for stochastic models. Different claim. INTRO-3 states it correctly.

INTRO-2, "Algorithm and code are one question." They are two questions the experimenter cannot separate. Collapsing them concedes that the paper cannot separate them either.

INTRO-3, "Every member is misspecified by construction." The full-covariance members are exact in the second moments; the misspecification is the Gaussian closure, unstated.

INTRO-2/INTRO-3, "two of them dimensionless" (INTRO-2: "two dimensionless"). A channel count is dimensionless. Three of them are.

INTRO-1/INTRO-2 attribute Münch's "state-dependent open-channel noise" without distinguishing it from the additive instrumental noise the design sweeps. The reader will assume they are the same axis.

**2. Rule violations**

R4, literal. INTRO-1: "with **only** the product of channel number and unitary current identified." The banned word, once. INTRO-2 and INTRO-3 paraphrase around it.

R8, rule-of-three triad. INTRO-1: "All of it is published, implemented and almost unused" (the source list has four items; the writer cut one to make a triad). INTRO-3: "All of it is published, available and almost unused." INTRO-2 keeps four and is clean.

R8, aphorism. INTRO-1: "Adopting one costs something." / "The apparatus is classical." INTRO-2: "Calibration is not adequacy." INTRO-3: "Standard practice discards it." / "A ladder followed." / "Something else changes as you climb."

R8, signposting. INTRO-2: "Least squares has survived for a reason worth conceding first."

R5, name it at most once. INTRO-3 mentions Moffatt and Pierdominici-Sottile in the ladder and again as "The boundary-conditioned likelihood is one more tool."

R3. INTRO-2/INTRO-3: "Least squares becomes calibrated once instrumental noise exceeds gating noise." A threshold verb on what the paper insists is a level set.

Length, hard range 800 to 900: INTRO-2 is 903 words. INTRO-1 is 900 exactly. INTRO-3 is 894.

**3. Attribution**

INTRO-2, "stationary Lorentzian spectra gave a unitary conductance and a closing rate with standard errors on both (Katz & Miledi 1970, 1972; Anderson & Stevens 1973)." INTRO-3 lumps identically. The joint estimate with standard errors is Anderson and Stevens; Katz and Miledi did not report it. INTRO-1 separates them correctly and is the only one that does.

INTRO-2/INTRO-3 drop the 256 to 504 sweeps. That number is the whole "validity, never absence" defence, and losing it weakens R7 compliance to an assertion.

INTRO-3, "a filter linear in the record" reads as a linear filter, not linear cost.

**4. Verdict**

Most defensible: INTRO-3, on substance. Cleanest citation of Owen, correct validity sentence, no banned "only". It is held back by the false events-per-sample regime claim and the aphoristic register.

Most exposed: INTRO-1. It opens on a wrong premise, contradicts its own design in the same page, uses the one word R4 bans, and manufactures a triad by deleting a fact. INTRO-2 is over the hard word cap, which disqualifies it before any of this is read.

readings.reading:
1. "Most macroscopic patch-clamp records sit in neither regime: a few hundred to a few thousand channels, openings unresolvable, averaging incomplete." That is my patch, described from the inside. Up to there I was reading about someone else's field, single channels or squid axons. That sentence said the paper was about mine.

2. "At the true parameters the score, the gradient of the log-likelihood, averages to zero over replicate recordings, and its covariance across them equals the Fisher information the likelihood reports." I have never computed a score. The inline definition did not rescue it, and I spent the rest of that sentence skimming for a word I owned. I came back at "the simulator supplies ground truth," which I understood immediately.

3. What I heard promised: my least squares point estimates are probably fine and my error bars are probably not, and the paper will show me where on a map of channel count, sampling rate and noise that goes from mildly wrong to badly wrong. Plus one number I can compute from my own residual without recording an ensemble I will never record. I half believe it. The map is built on a two-state scheme at open probability one half and my scheme is not, though the lower-bound line partly covers me. What cost the most belief was the last sentence, "Which to prefer, and when, is not settled here." I was shown a map and then told the destination is withheld.

4. The roster paragraph, Milescu through Moffatt and Pierdominici-Sottile. Seven methods, one sentence each, none of them sitting in my analysis. I could not hold them in order, and the "two axes" sentence that would have organised the list came after the list was over. I would have skipped to the next paragraph and lost nothing.

5. "Ignoring the correlation usually leaves the point estimate standing while corrupting the count of independent residuals behind every confidence interval." I have published those intervals, from records exactly like the ones described. The other one that landed was "whether the scheme is right, wrong, or the code broken." I have suspected my own code and had no way to check it.

I kept reading at "Most macroscopic recordings sit between: a few hundred to a few thousand channels, individual openings unresolvable, averaging incomplete." That is my patch. The literature I get is either single-channel dwell times or Hodgkin-Huxley, and I work in the gap between them without anyone naming it. The sentence right after, that channel number and unitary current enter the mean as a product, landed too, because I have papered over that with a separate single-channel estimate for twenty years and always felt slightly dishonest doing it.

My attention dropped at "Whole-record likelihoods keep different amounts:" and I skimmed to the end of the semicolons. Eight methods, each with a qualifying clause, none of which I can hold in my head. It reads like a related-work section dropped into the middle of an argument I was following.

What I think you promised: you will tell me whether the confidence interval my least-squares fit prints is the interval it actually delivers, and you will give me something I can compute on the residual I already have to find out where my own experiment sits. Do I believe it? About half. Two states at open probability one half is nobody's channel, but you say so and call it a lower bound, and I accept that. The last sentence promises "one measurement on the reader's own residual" without saying what it is. If it turns out to need an ensemble of replicate recordings, which you just told me is out of reach, I will feel taken.

I would have skipped the "Correlation-based kinetics is not new" paragraph entirely. First clause, then jump.

Implicated twice. "Ignoring the correlation usually leaves the point estimate intact; what it damages is the count of independent residuals, the number turning a residual sum of squares into a confidence interval." Those are the intervals I publish. And then "Least squares becomes calibrated once instrumental noise exceeds gating noise," followed by the rank deficiency, which says my noisy recordings, the ones I apologise for, are the honest ones and my clean ones are where I fool myself.

The random-walk model that predicts perfectly and knows nothing also stuck.

I stayed with it from "channel number and unitary current enter it as a product no fit to the mean can separate." That is the thing I have argued about with reviewers for years, and here it was offered as the reason to care about the wiggle I have always treated as noise to be averaged down.

My attention dropped at "at the true parameters the score, the gradient of the log-likelihood, averages to zero over replicate recordings, and its covariance across them equals the Fisher information the likelihood reports." I have never computed a score. The parenthetical names told me this was a paragraph for someone else, and I read the rest of it at speed without taking anything in.

What I understood the promise to be: a map that tells me which of these fitting methods is trustworthy at my number of channels and my sampling rate, and whether the error bars I already report are honest. I half believe I will get it. The scheme is two-state at open probability one half, and mine is not, so I expect to be told my case is worse without being told how much worse. The last paragraph also admits that the identity behind all of it needs replicate recordings I do not have, and then offers me "one measurement on my own residual," which sounds smaller than what the earlier paragraphs led me to want.

I would have skipped the paragraph beginning with Lorentzian spectra. I do not do stationary noise analysis, the citations are all older than my career, and by the third one I was scanning for the next paragraph break. I nearly skipped the ladder paragraph too, seven names in a row, though the last sentence of it saved it because it told me what actually varies along the list.

Two sentences felt like they were about me. "The point estimate often survives; the count of independent residuals that turns a residual sum of squares into a confidence interval does not." And "Least squares becomes calibrated once instrumental noise exceeds gating noise, its interval matching the spread delivered, though its information matrix is rank deficient there." That second one made me want to know which side of that line my recordings sit on, and I could not tell from what I had read.

readings.thread: C: the enemy inside the weapon
readings.reading:
The sentence that got me was "Most macroscopic recordings sit in neither place: a few hundred to a few thousand channels, with openings unresolvable and averaging incomplete." That is my patch. I have spent years in a regime I had quietly filed as "single channel, but too many," and seeing it named as its own place made me want the rest.

My attention dropped at "Milescu, Akk & Sachs (2005) keep the gating variance at every sample and drop the dependence between samples." From there through Stepanyuk and Münch I was skimming names. I do not use any of these methods, so an ordering among them is an argument between other people. It came back briefly at "almost unused," because that matched my experience, then went again at "Three quantities set position on the map, two of them dimensionless."

What I take as the promise: my least-squares fits give roughly the right rate constants, my error bars on them are probably wrong, and this paper will tell me by how much and in which direction for an experiment like mine, plus give me something I can compute on residuals I already have. I half believe it. The measurement-against-exact-simulation logic I follow and find convincing. The delivery to me is the part I doubt, because it arrives in the last paragraph in the vaguest language in the whole introduction, and because the test case is two states at open probability one half while my schemes have six.

The paragraph I would have skipped is the genealogy one, Katz and Miledi through Moffatt and Pierdominici-Sottile. On a first pass I would have jumped from "fitting the mean" straight to what goes wrong.

Implicated, twice. "the approaches surveyed by Clerx et al. (2019) are deterministic with a root-mean-square objective" put my software in the sentence. Then "Ignoring the correlation leaves the point estimate intact; what it damages is the count of independent residuals that turns a residual sum of squares into a confidence interval." I have written those intervals into grants. That one landed physically.

The closing sentence, that when each is preferable is not settled here, took some of it back.

The sentence where I stopped skimming: "Channel number and unitary current enter the mean as a product, so no fit to the mean separates them; what separates them is in the fluctuation." I have had that argument with a reviewer. I fixed N by other means and moved on. Seeing the fluctuation named as the thing that does the separating made me want the rest.

My attention dropped at "At the true parameters the score, the gradient of the log-likelihood, averages to zero across replicate recordings, and its covariance equals the Fisher information the likelihood reports for itself." I read it three times. The definition is right there and I still could not tell whether this was a test I could run on my recordings or one that only a simulation study can run. Two paragraphs later I found out it's mostly the second.

What I think I was promised: my least-squares confidence intervals are too narrow because the residuals are correlated, the paper will say how much too narrow and where on a map of channel number, sampling interval and noise it bites, and it will give me one thing to compute from my own residuals so I can find myself on that map. The first two I believe. The third I will believe when I see it. The ensemble requirement is conceded to be something I don't have, and "we hand back one measurement on their residual" is the vaguest sentence in the piece.

I skipped the lineage paragraph, Conti and Sigworth through Moffatt and Pierdominici-Sottile. At reading speed it is a list of names, and the two axes at the end carry the point without it.

Implicated, twice. "Ignoring the correlation rarely moves the point estimate; it moves the count of independent residuals that turns a residual sum of squares into a confidence interval." That is my Table 1. And "all four approaches surveyed by Clerx et al. (2019) use a root-mean-square objective," which is a polite way of saying that everyone whose code I trust does what I do. The line about a model with no kinetics passing both checks landed too, though it reads as a warning about the likelihoods I don't use.
